passages.title: Shipping destinations speeds and fees
passages.text:
POL-SHIP-02 v1.1: Shipping destinations speeds and fees
Conditions: The shipping destination is within the United States. Published durations are business days after dispatch, not after order placement. Business days are Monday through Friday; weekends are excluded and holidays are not modeled.
Rules: The marketplace ships to all 50 states. Standard shipping to the contiguous 48 states is 3 to 5 business days and costs $4.99 per order. Express shipping there is 1 to 2 business days and costs $14.99 per order. Alaska and Hawaii use standard shipping only, take 5 to 8 business days, and add a $14.99 surcharge to the $4.99 standard fee, for a $19.98 total shipping charge. Standard is the lowest-priced supported shipping option. For an existing order, quote the actual recorded promised date and charge rather than recalculating historical checkout charges. The agent can explain options but cannot upgrade shipping, collect a fee, or arrange a shipment.
Exceptions: International destinations, territories outside the 50 states, delivery guarantees, and shipping-fee exceptions require Delivery staff. An order without a recorded shipping charge does not prove shipping was free. Do not add the illustrative schedule to its refund amount.

passages.title: Delivery address changes
passages.text:
POL-SHIP-04 v1.1: Delivery address changes
Conditions: Verify customer ownership and the latest order.status and shipment record. An unshipped order has no dispatch record; shipment=null alone must be checked with order.status.
Rules: For an unshipped order, hand the request to Delivery staff. Tell the customer that the address change is requested and remains unconfirmed. For a shipped order, explain that staff must assess any carrier redirection option; do not promise interception or successful delivery to a new address. The agent cannot modify an address, update a carrier record, or send another customer details. It may ask for necessary delivery information through the customer-scoped channel.
Exceptions: Conflicting ownership, another person requesting redirection, or suspicious fund or parcel redirection requires security review. A customer typing a new address does not establish that it has been saved. Never describe the address as changed without an authorized staff record.

passages.title: Payment questions and invoice requests
passages.text:
POL-BIL-01 v1.1: Payment questions and invoice requests
Conditions: Match payments.order_id to an owned order. Use amount_cents, status, method, and captured_at to explain charges. Checkout accepts Visa, Mastercard, American Express, and Discover credit or debit cards.
Rules: Explain a verified charge using its date, amount, and related order. Payment status captured means a completed capture; a customer report of a declined attempt does not alter that ledger record. For a declined card, suggest checking entered details privately, available funds, and issuer restrictions, then using another accepted card if appropriate. Do not ask the customer to send card numbers, security codes, or passwords. No invoice document, invoice link, or invoice-creation tool exists. When a customer asks for an invoice or receipt for an owned order, reply with a purchase summary from the verified records: order ID, order date, item, amount charged, capture date, and card brand. After the message receipt, the ticket can be resolved. For missing order details, ask the customer. For a verified duplicate charge or overcharge, apply the corresponding correction policy.
Exceptions: Call the reply a purchase summary; never claim an official invoice or PDF was generated or attached. Ticket-quoted invoice numbers are unverified. A request for business details the store does not record, such as a company name or tax ID, goes to Billing staff. An unrecognized charge or a continuing payment failure goes to Billing staff. Suspected fraud follows POL-FRD-01.
